verdict.reasoning: Patient says: "I've had a sort of fairly sort of bad, severe headache for the past four days."
Same as cc-001: "severe headache for the past four days."
Patient describes feeling hot with suspected fever and later confirms hot and cold: "I've been sort of feeling a bit hot as well... I think I've got fever" and doctor summarizes "Hot and cold. Yeah."

Rash description: "It's rashes kind of all over my body... Sort of red and itchy." Doctor confirms it blanches: "if you put a glass on top of the rash, does that rash go away?" Patient: "Yes, it goes away."
Patient reports generalized muscle/body aches: "I've got sort of general aching muscles... it's kind of a bit all over" and "Just I suppose, general aching, body aching."

Doctor asks about neck movement pain: "Is there any pain when you try to move your neck..." Patient: "Not necessary, sort of in my neck. It's kind of a bit all over, really." Neck stiffness is not explicitly discussed or denied; inferring denial of neck stiffness is not clearly stated.
Photophobia denied: Doctor: "do you find it difficult to look at the light?" Patient: "No, it's fine. Light doesn't seem to bother me too much."
Doctor: "have you been sick with this headache?" Patient: "No, I haven't been sick." This supports denial of vomiting; nausea is not mentioned but commonly implied with “been sick” in this context.

Cough and earache are denied, but sore throat is never discussed. Transcript: Doctor: "do you have a cough?" Patient: "No, no cough." and "your ears are okay? There's no earaches?" Patient: "No". No mention of sore throat.

Doctor asks about paresthesia and weakness: "have you experienced any pins and needles in your face, arms and legs?" Patient: "No, no pins and needles." and clarification about weakness: "Not any weakness, but where you couldn't, you know, hold a cup..." Patient: "Seem to be fine with that sort of stuff."
Patient: "I have been away to Thailand a week or so ago. I've had some like usual mosquito bites from sort of traveling around."
Patient: "and a friend of mine has also been a bit unwell."
Past medical/surgical history: Doctor: "do you suffer from any medical conditions?" Patient: "No, general medical history is fine." Doctor: "no surgical history..." Patient: "No."
Patient: "So I've had some paracetamol... but it's not really helping at the moment."
Same sentence: "I've had some paracetamol and some ibuprofen, but it's not really helping at the moment."
Doctor: "are you on any regular, any medication, anything that you're using at all?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "Any allergies at all?" Patient: "No." This supports no known drug allergies.

Doctor states exam cannot be done online: "I believe that it is quite important for us to actually examine you... it's not possible for us to do that online. I think you would need to come into one of our hubs." No physical exam findings are documented.
Patient says they have not measured their temperature: "I haven't measured it, but I think I've got fever." Afebrile by measurement is not established, as no measurement was taken.
Doctor confirms a blanching rash: "if you put a glass on top of the rash, does that rash go away?" Patient: "Yes, it goes away."

Clinician discusses acute illness after travel with headache, rash, myalgia: mentions possible viral illness after Thailand travel and notes "you just have a general muscle ache" plus blanching rash and suspected fever. This summarizes the presentation described.
Doctor: "things that's running in the back of my mind are kind of viral illnesses that one can get with sort of mosquito bites or foreign travel."
Doctor: "The other common thing around Thailand, it will be like some dengue..." This explicitly includes dengue (an arbovirus) in the differential.

Doctor: "we have to rule out is meningitis... you didn't say that you had problems looking at light" and explains "in meningitis, you get a non blanching rash, while in any kind of virus... the rash usually goes away." Neck stiffness is not explicitly restated but the reasoning reflects lower concern due to absence of classic signs including photophobia and non-blanching rash.
Doctor: "we need to do is to urgently examine you, and that's sometime today... I'd like you to be seen in one of our hubs as soon as possible... preferably in the next few hours time."
Doctor: "maybe have some blood tests and examinations."
Doctor: "if that's not available, I'd like you to take yourself to A E."
